name: Remote fleet sweep that may only ever open a DRAFT pull request
description: Blueprint 42 of 96 (BP-IMP-05). Sweeps many repositories with autonomous remote runners under one hard structural constraint: the runner can open a DRAFT PR and nothing else. Merge tools are DENIED by policy rather than discouraged, so scale never buys the right to land unreviewed code. Two separately-scoped credentials are declared as distinct secret references - a dispatch credential that cannot read auth and a secrets credential that cannot trigger runs - and neither value ever travels in the task text or the export bundle. A sweep that produces no PRs is treated as a DETECTOR question before it is treated as a content result.

repo_targets.description: Enabled targets from the targets file. An empty list is a configuration fault, not an empty sweep.

per_repo_task.description: The single change every runner attempts. Must be verifiable by that repo's own CI or the repo is skipped.

dispatch_credential.description: Reference name only. Scope: trigger the runner workflow. It must NOT be able to read auth or write secrets.

secrets_credential.description: Reference name only. Scope: write repository Secrets for token refresh. It must NOT be able to trigger runs. The split IS the security design; a single shared-scope credential defeats it.

off_peak_window.description: A daytime sweep can silently starve interactive quota on the shared subscription

sweep_deadline_seconds.description: Wall-clock bound on the whole sweep; late runners are reported as late, never dropped

target-selector.description: Reads the targets file and emits the enabled set; refuses to invent targets when the file is empty

remote-runner.description: One remote job per repository. Makes the change, runs that repo's own CI, opens a DRAFT PR, and stops.
write_paths: the target repository working tree only

sweep-auditor.description: Answers 'why did this sweep produce N PRs' as a DETECTOR question first - targets enabled, credential valid, runner log present - before treating N as a content result

owner.description: The ONLY actor that may merge. Every PR from this workflow waits here.

routes.reason: the auditor must not share a vendor with the runners whose silence it is diagnosing

draft-only.expression: every_pr_is_draft == true AND auto_merged_prs == 0 AND force_pushes == 0

credential-scopes-split.expression: dispatch_scope_can_read_auth == false AND secrets_scope_can_trigger_runs == false AND credential_values_in_task_text == 0

empty-sweep-is-a-detector-question.expression: targets_enabled_checked == true AND dispatch_credential_authenticated == true AND runner_logs_present == true

stages.title: S0 SELECT the enabled targets - an empty targets file is a fault, not a result

work_unit.title: Enumerate the enabled fleet targets and prove the propose-only owner gate cannot be bypassed on any of them
work_unit.question_or_target: Read the targets file, emit the enabled repository set, and for each target enumerate every route by which a runner could land code without owner approval - direct push, auto-merge, ready-for-review plus a merge queue, an admin override - and confirm each is closed. An empty enabled set is reported as FAILED, never as a clean sweep of zero.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the owner-gate enumeration is a security judgement, not a lookup

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the enabled target list with, per target, the branch-protection and auto-merge settings read from the API - a claim that merging is blocked must cite the setting that blocks it
tests_required: an empty enabled set must emit FAILED, not SUCCESS with zero targets
a target whose repository allows auto-merge must be reported as an OPEN bypass route before any dispatch
both-states control: a repo with branch protection ON and one with it OFF must produce different verdicts; identical verdicts mean the setting was never read
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: an independent reviewer who re-reads the protection settings from the API for a sample of targets rather than trusting the emitted set
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:ADV-0140 emitted only when target-set.json exists, parses, is non-empty, and every target carries its measured bypass-route verdict; otherwise FAILED:ADV-0140 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot; a second empty read means the targets file or the credential is wrong - diagnose the detector, do not retry the read

stages.title: The two credential scopes must be genuinely disjoint before anything is dispatched
S1-S3 One remote runner per repo: change, that repo's own CI, DRAFT PR

body.title: Make the change and run THAT repository's CI - not ours
A repo whose CI cannot verify the change is SKIPPED, never force-pushed
Open a DRAFT pull request and stop - this is the terminal action a runner may take

stages.title: Every PR must still be a draft when the sweep ends
S4a Why did the sweep produce N PRs? Detector first, content second
An empty sweep may not be reported as success until the detector is cleared
S4 ROLL UP - a no-op repo gets an explicit no-op record, not an absence
Only the owner merges. The sweep ends here by design.
stages.prompt: These draft PRs are ready for human review. Review burden is the declared cost of this blueprint: the runners cannot merge, cannot mark ready, and cannot force-push. Approve, request changes, or close.

impact.blast_radius: one draft PR per target repository; nothing is merged, so reverting the sweep means closing the drafts

worked_example.no_op_case: repo 14 already satisfies the floor. The runner opens NO PR and writes an explicit no-op record; roll-up-dashboard reports it as no-op, so 25 PRs against 26 targets is not a silent gap
worked_example.revoked_credential_case: the dispatch credential is revoked before the run. Every runner fails to trigger and zero PRs appear. WITHOUT yield-gate this reads as 'nothing needed changing'; WITH it, empty-sweep-is-a-detector-question fails on dispatch_credential_authenticated == false and the sweep is reported as a DETECTOR failure
worked_example.unverifiable_ci_case: repo 21 has no CI that exercises the changed path. ci-gate fails, the repo is recorded as SKIPPED, and no PR is opened - the alternative (push and hope) is what the gate exists to prevent
worked_example.quota_case: run overnight because a daytime sweep on the shared subscription starves interactive coding with 429s; off_peak_window=immediate is available but is not the default
worked_example.credential_handling: both credentials are declared as secret_ref params: the workflow carries the reference NAME, the value is never in the task text, and export.redact_secrets is true so the bundle cannot carry it either

x_extensions.distinctive_mechanism: propose-only as a POLICY property - merge tooling is in tool_policy.deny, ready-for-review requires owner approval - plus two disjoint credential scopes and a deadline barrier that reports late runners rather than dropping them
contraindications: NOT for a single repository - local is cheaper and the remote machinery buys nothing
NOT for changes needing deep repo-specific judgement - the same task text cannot fit 26 repos
NOT when the change cannot be verified by the target repo's own CI - such repos are skipped by gate, not pushed
x_extensions.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-IMP-06 fans many WORK UNITS onto rented compute for a RAM ceiling; this fans one task across many REPOSITORIES on their own CI, and its defining property is that the runner's terminal action is a draft PR.
